titles.title: On endomorphisms of affine spaces and the Jacobian problem

rightsList.rights: Creative Commons Attribution Non Commercial No Derivatives 4.0 International

descriptions.description: Let $p$ be a prime. We provide examples which show that étale endomorphisms of affine planes over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p$ can have fibers of arbitrary finite cardinal. Let $(l,m)\in\mathbb N\times\mathbb N^{\ast}$. We provide examples of such étale endomorphisms whose images have complements of cardinality $l$ and whose geometric degrees are $pm$. Several conjectures are disproved, and in particular we provide an analog over $k$ of Kulikov's counterexample to the `Generalized Jacobian Conjecture' of Bass for surfaces. Surjective (resp.\ surjective and non-surjective) counterexamples to Adjamagbo's Jacobian Conjecture over each $k$ are included in dimension $2$ (resp.\ in all dimensions at least $3$); for instance, if $p=2$, then we show for each $m$ there exist surjective étale endomorphisms of the affine spaces over $k$ of dimension at least $3$ of geometric degree $m$. If $e:X\rightarrow X$ is an endomorphism of a variety over an algebraically closed field $K$, then we show that there exists $n\in\mathbb N$ such that $\Imm(e^n)=\Imm(e^{n+1})$ provided either (i) $e$ is quasi-finite or (ii) $\dim(X)\le 2$ and $X\setminus\Imm(e)$ is finite. We provide examples of endomorphisms of affine planes of dimensions at least $3$ over $K$ whose images have complements of cardinality $l$ and for all $n\in\mathbb N$ we have $\Imm(e^n)\neq\Imm(e^{n+1})$. We prove that all affine moduli schemes of étale endomorphisms of affine spaces with Jacobian matrices of determinant 1 over $K$ are connected and classify all those that are smooth. We prove that the Jacobian Conjecture over $\mathbb C$ and Adjamagbo's analog of it over $k$ hold for étale endomorphisms of affine spaces that are composites $g\circ f$, where $f$ is quasi-finite and a locally closed embedding in codimension $1$ outside a specific finite subset and $g$ is a projection that omits one coordinate.
175 pages. Version 356

titles.title: A Short Resolution of Zhao's Open Problem 5.2 after the 2026 Jacobian Counterexample

descriptions.description: Zhao asked in 2008 whether the Vanishing Conjecture can fail for a nonpolynomial Hessian-nilpotent formal power series over C. The 2026 failure of the Jacobian Conjecture, combined with Zhao's 2007 equivalence, supplies a homogeneous quartic Hessian-nilpotent polynomial P0 for which the Vanishing Conjecture fails. We adjoin two fresh variables and a nonpolynomial isotropic tail R=q(u+iv). Zhao's own disjoint-sum identity then gives exact additivity of Delta^m P^(m+1), while every power of R is harmonic. Hence P0+R is a nonpolynomial Hessian-nilpotent formal power series for which the Vanishing Conjecture fails. This closes Open Problem 5.2. The mechanism is principally a post-2026 corollary of Zhao's published machinery; priority is not claimed.

titles.title: A quadratic family of integral two-torsion classes in a Huneke-Wiegand Koszul presentation

descriptions.description:
For every integer p>=8, we prove that an explicit integral Koszul presentation associated with a previously constructed Huneke-Wiegand family has a direct summand (Z/2)^q, where q=floor(((p-2)^2+3)/12). The classes are indexed by the strictly increasing nonnegative triples i<j<k with i+j+k=p-2. Reflection-symmetric interval potentials give complete original-domain integer sources for twice each class; relative parity functionals with ten to twelve supporting K rows detect the classes independently. An elementary six-step counting argument gives the quadratic growth, and a vector-space extension argument gives the splitting. No explicit uniform global retraction or complete Smith form is claimed.
The proof includes an exhaustive classification of every source that can meet the functionals and a complete reconstruction of the D-kernel in every relevant high-variable sector, including the free diagonal potentials at the endpoint sector. It also proves exact order two for a previously tracked four-row connecting representative, constructs its original signed annihilator and its transfer to one triangle class, and gives a complete integral potential basis of rank binomial(p-1,2) in a neighboring sector with at most seven K rows per basis image.
Independent exact audits verify all 70 declared triangle sources, five representative-transfer identities, and 364 complete triangle-sector parity certificates at p=8,...,12. These certificates concern 27 functionals on 65 distinct sectors containing 23,695 distinct original S sources; repeated sector incidences are not counted as distinct matrices. Separate campaigns check 861 neighboring-sector chains, 18 full annihilators, and 2,123 complete-kernel potential chains. Every tested signed source is preserved in deterministic lossless archives. The uniform theorems follow from the complete symbolic proofs, not extrapolation from these finite checks.
Scope: this is a partial direct-summand decomposition of the full explicit integral presentation, not a classification of its entire cokernel, an upper bound, an identification with an isolated or relative-completion quotient, or a proof of the lower-strand recurrence. The family-to-presentation identification is an explicitly imported premise. Son Pham retains priority for the original public counterexample; this is a separate homological companion to the CAOS family record. The Jacobian conjecture is not addressed. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

titles.title: kellermap: certified reductions of polynomial Keller maps

descriptions.description:
kellermap constructs and verifies reductions of polynomial maps with constantJacobian determinant. Every transformation is a certificate object that carriesits own obligations; verification names the obligation that failed rather thanreturning a boolean, and a collision is transported across each step andre-verified, so that a reduction of a counterexample is still a counterexample.

Version 0.6 implements the second and third stages of the Bass-Connell-WrightReduction Theorem, collision-hull compression, and the symmetric lift to thegradient form of a quartic over a field containing i. Applied in sequence tothe smallest degree-three map this project holds, the chain runs 11, 22, 23,19, 38 variables with every step verified and the collision arriving at thefar end.

The constructions are other people's. What this project contributes is thecomposition of them, the certificates, and eight reconstruction scripts thatrecompute the published results in plain SymPy without using the library. Nominimality and no priority is claimed for any figure: both figures this chainreaches were published elsewhere first, by a different route, and the recordof what this project claimed too widely and corrected is in `docs/errata.md`.

Generative AI tools were used in two roles: one model wrote code, tests anddocumentation in conversation with the maintainer, and a different modelaudited the release candidates. `docs/provenance.md` names the tools, says whateach did, and records what the arrangement found -- six audits, of which thefirst five each turned up faults that the test suite, the coverage requirementand a forty-two-probe mutation sweep had all passed. Neither model is anauthor. The maintainer set the tasks, ran the gates, read the deliveries anddecided what entered the repository.

descriptions.description: Anonymous, AI-assisted, unrefereed computer-assisted candidate. Exact five-support exclusion, tangent multiplicity-six nullcone containment, three rational localized-colon elements, and sixteen exact rational source-module syzygies in a frozen fourth Macaulay block. titles.title: A Relative Jacobian-Rank Filtration for Keller Maps

descriptions.description: We introduce the relative Jacobian rank rho_rel(F), the minimum over complex basepoints of the generic rank of JF(x)-JF(a). For complex Keller maps we prove that rho_rel(F) <= 1 implies polynomial automorphy. Consequently every hypothetical nonautomorphic planar Keller map has rho_rel=2. We show that rank two is the first relative-rank stratum permitting nontrivial determinant-balance cancellation and certify rho_rel=3 for an explicit three-dimensional noninjective Keller map from the 2026 counterexample literature. The paper does not claim rho_rel(F) <= 2 implies automorphism. Exact symbolic verification is supplementary.

descriptions.description:
This paper presents a rigorous mathematical proof of the complex-field Jacobianconjecture. The conjecture states that if �:ℂ� → ℂ� is a polynomial mapping whoseJacobian determinant is a non-zero constant over the entire domain, then � must bea polynomial automorphism of ℂ�. The proof is established based on fundamentalcomplex algebraic geometry, homogeneous decomposition of polynomial mappings,and the global invertibility of Jacobian matrices. By means of asymptotic analysis atinfinity and proof by contradiction, we eliminate the geometric possibility of noncompact fibers and establish the non-existence of escape sequences at infinity. titles.title: Divisors in projective bundles over the projective line whose complement is affine space

descriptions.description: Given a smooth projective variety $X$ of dimension $n$ and a closed subscheme $Z \subseteq X$, it is in general a difficult problem to determine whether $X \setminus Z$ is isomorphic to $\mathbf A^n$. In the case where $X$ is a projective bundle over $\mathbf P^1$ and the restriction of every irreducible component of $Z$ to every fibre is a hyperplane, we give a complete geometric characterisation in terms of the irreducible components of $Z$ and their intersections. In the appendix, we use this to obtain a coordinate-free explanation for the recent first counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture.
12 pages. Comments are welcome!

titles.title: On the Jacobian Conjecture and the Nilpotent Tree Inversion of Keller Mappings

descriptions.description:
This preprint provides an exhaustive mathematical monograph on Smale's 16th Problem (Steve Smale, 2000), dedicated to the celebrated Jacobian Conjecture originally posed by Ott-Heinrich Keller in 1939.

The conjecture asserts that if a polynomial mapping F = (F1, …, Fn) : &complex;n → &complex;n has a non-zero constant Jacobian determinant det Jac(F)(x) ∈ &complex;* for all x ∈ &complex;n, then F is a global polynomial automorphism of &complex;n (i.e. globally bijective with a polynomial inverse):

det Jac(F)(x) = 1 &implies; F ∈ Aut(&complex;[x1, …, xn])

This 11-page treatise presents an algebraic and geometric survey encompassing the Bialynicki-Birula & Rosenlicht injectivity theorem, Pinchuk's counterexample in the real case ℝ2, the Bass-Connell-Wright cubic- nilpotent reduction, Drużkowski matrix Jordan stratifications, the formal tree expansion inverse formula, and the Kontsevich-Dixmier Weyl algebra equivalence.

Key Mathematical Results & Contributions



Axiomatic Formulation & Dimension 1 Proof: Rigorous proof that in dimension n = 1, Keller mappings reduce to degree-1 affine bijections F(x) = ax + b with polynomial inverse F−1(y) = (y − b)/a.

Bass-Connell-Wright (1982) & Yagzhev (1980) Cubic Reduction: Complete derivation showing that the Jacobian Conjecture in all dimensions is equivalent to the invertibility of cubic-homogeneous mappings F(x) = x − H(x) where Jac(H) is strictly nilpotent of index n.

Drużkowski Cubic-Linear Factorization: Structural analysis of H(x) = (Ax)*3 and Jordan nilpotent strata for the coefficient matrix A.

Wright Nilpotent Tree Inversion Formula: Explicit combinatorial sum of rooted differential operator trees proving that the formal inverse series F−1(y) truncates into a finite polynomial of degree at most 3n−1 under Jacobian nilpotency.

Kontsevich & Dixmier Equivalence: Detailed exposition of the Kontsevich–Belov-Kanel–Tsuchimoto theorem establishing that the Jacobian Conjecture in dimension 2n is equivalent to the Dixmier Conjecture on the Weyl algebra An(&complex;).

100% Machine-Checked Verification in Lean 4: Invertibility lemmas, triangular polynomial automorphisms, exact quadratic/cubic tree inversion formulas, and nilpotent operator algebras are formally certified with 0 axioms, 0 linter warnings, and 0 sorry placeholders via the Lean 4 interactive theorem prover and Mathlib.


Repository and Verification Artifacts

The companion machine-checked code and formal verification artifacts are publicly hosted on GitHub:https://github.com/flouzzy/smale-problemsInteractive Portal: https://maths-proofs.edounze.com/#smale-16-jacobian

Primary MSC (2020): 14R15, 13B10, 14E07, 16S32, 68V20.Keywords: Jacobian Conjecture, Smale's 16th Problem, Keller Mappings, Polynomial Automorphisms, Bass-Connell-Wright Reduction, Drużkowski Matrices, Nilpotent Tree Inversion, Dixmier Conjecture, Formal Verification, Lean 4, Mathlib.

descriptions.description: This paper establishes two theorems that partition the Jacobian (Keller) conjecture into a solved region and an open boundary. Theorem A constructs an infinite family F_e : ℂ³ → ℂ³ of non-injective Keller maps with det(J) = −e for every nonzero integer e. The architecture is universal: the first two components constitute a fixed collapse engine independent of e; only the third scales linearly. Three universal collision points map to the same image for all values of e. The Alpöge–Fable counterexample (20 July 2026) is the special case e = 2. Theorem B proves that this projection-symmetry architecture cannot produce a Keller map in dimension 2: the projection consumes both coordinates, leaving no free variable to sustain a nonzero constant determinant. Theorem C establishes a rank boundary: rank-1 perturbations force triangularity and injectivity, while rank-2 permits non-triangularizable collisions. A conjecture of complete classification is stated: every counterexample in dimension n ≥ 3 is architecturally equivalent to a dimensional collapse by projection with collision symmetry. The structural principle — dimensional collapse under canonical projection, with the Jacobian as surviving invariant — was published by the author on 9 March 2026 (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18925135). All results are verified symbolically (SymPy) and formalized in Lean 4.

titles.title: The minimal equivariant counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture

descriptions.description:
Machine-certified classification of C*-equivariant Keller maps on C3. We prove that Alpöge's degree-7 counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture is degree-minimal within its full equivariant class: every C*-equivariant Keller map of total degree at most 6 for weights (−1,1,2) is a polynomial automorphism. The same rigidity holds through degree 6 for weight systems (−1,1,3) and (−1,1,4).
For every k ≥ 2 and weights (−1,1,k) we prove the quotient identity det Dφ = −Ek det JF, machine-checked in Lean 4 uniformly in k, which drives the equivariant degree search across the family.
All computations are exact (rational arithmetic). Gröbner-basis certificates (msolve, cross-checked in Singular) accompany the paper.

titles.title: teerthsharma/monodromy: monodromy v0.1.0 — injectivity without the Jacobian

descriptions.description:
Deciding injectivity, symmetry, dimension and sensitivity from multi-point
geometry rather than from the Jacobian determinant.

Motivation

The working invertibility certificate across applied machine learning is local:
sample the domain, evaluate det DF, and conclude invertibility if it never
vanishes or never changes sign. This inference underwrites the change-of-variables
density in normalizing flows, the folding check in diffeomorphic image
registration, and element validity in mesh generation.

The forward implication is the inverse function theorem and is sound. The
converse — local invertibility everywhere implying global injectivity — is what
fails. The Jacobian conjecture (Keller, 1939) asked whether a polynomial map of
C^n with det DF a nonzero constant must be a polynomial automorphism. It was
refuted in July 2026; arXiv:2608.00222 (Gao, 31 July 2026) generalises the
refutation above dimension two and describes the counterexamples as "everywhere
unramified, and fail to be injective only through points escaping to infinity" —
étale coverings that are not proper. JC_2 remains open.

Under a hypothesis that is now known to be insufficient, a certificate reading
one point at a time cannot decide the question. This release provides
certificates that read more than one point.

Principal results

Jacobian-free injectivity. Define

free_ratio(F; X) = [ min_{p≠q} |F(p)−F(q)| / |p−q| ]
                 ÷ [ median_{p≠q} |F(p)−F(q)| / |p−q| ]

Numerator and denominator are distances between sampled points; no derivative is
evaluated. On eight maps with closed-form ground truth drawn from the settings
above, the determinant test scores 6/8 and this statistic 8/8, separating
the classes by a factor of 3.02 (injective 1.53e-02 … 7.06e-01; non-injective
1.04e-03 … 5.07e-03). The two determinant failures are exactly those the
refutation predicts: a planar flow layer with w·u = −2, whose det DF = 1 − 2 sech²(z) is strictly positive for |z| > 0.8814 while g(z) = z − 2 tanh z
gives g(1.915) = g(−1.915) = 0; and a log-polar registration map with
det = e^{2x} > 0 satisfying F(x,y) = F(x, y+2π).

A normalisation branching on the hypothesis. ρ = λ/s with s = min σ_min(DF)
uses the determinant as reference rather than answer. It is valid only where F
is étale, since it divides by a quantity vanishing exactly under ramification;
the decision branches on min|det| / median|det|.

Properness as a growth exponent, and the covering chain. With
m(R) = min_{|x|=R} |F(x)|, F is proper iff m(R) → ∞. A proper local
homeomorphism is a covering map; its image is open and closed, hence the whole
connected target; C^n is simply connected, so the covering is trivial and the
degree is 1. Hence étale ∧ proper ⟹ injective. Both estimator traps are
documented: a sampled sphere minimum cannot locate a zero on a measure-zero
subvariety (unrefined sampling reports a clean exponent of 1.000 for a map whose
m(R) is identically 0), and the exponent alone remains insufficient after
refinement because a numerical floor times R has the same slope.

A certified proof on convex regions. For x, y ∈ B convex,
F(y) − F(x) = M(y − x) with M in the entrywise interval hull of DF over B;
0 ∉ [det] proves injectivity on B. Measured: 3 proofs, 0 false certificates
across 7 adversarial cases, at 0.0017 s against 3.5 s for the sampled certificate.
This is classical interval analysis — Lagrange, Delanoue & Jaulin, Reliable
Computing 13 (2007), Theorems 5 and 7 — and is included with that attribution.

Symmetry: periodicity is not symmetry. harmonic_order establishes that a
defect profile repeats with period 360/n; it does not establish that the defect
at 360/n is small. make_swiss_roll(400, random_state=0)[:, :2] was reported
C2 at power 0.8897 in four of six configurations. The discriminator is the
sample's own mean nearest-neighbour spacing (true symmetries 0.0000–1.6223, false
positives 2.3737–2.8243). Depth below the profile median was measured and rejected
at a separation of 1.013.

Thresholds as minimax equilibria. V(t) = max(FN(t), FP(t)), t* = argmin V.
Reported with the negative result that the game value is 0.000 for every
separable statistic and therefore cannot rank a gap of factor 3.01 against one of
1.01; the margin can, and maximising the minimum margin is the same minimax
problem.

Verification



Mutation score 15/15. Fifteen deliberate reversions of real fixes, applied
one at a time from an isolated git worktree, each required to turn the suite
red. Three survived an earlier pass and were bound, including one that the
trace identity Σλ = ln|det| provably could not detect because the mutation
conserves it.

116 passed, 5 xfailed, 0 failed.

Clean-room install, independently audited: wheel into a fresh virtualenv,
imported from a working directory with the source tree absent from sys.path,
under numpy 2.4.6; all entry points executed on 25,934 real exchange trades;
map_spectrum called, Σλ = ln(0.3) to 15 digits; torch absent from
pip list, from sys.modules, and import torch raises.

Hénon reference check: λ₁ = +0.42084 against Sprott's +0.41922,
D_KY = 1.25901 against 1.25827.

Sierpinski gasket: 1.5998 against exact log 3 / log 2 = 1.5850.


Limitations

Stated in docs/corrections.md and in each module rather than implied by
omission. Only the box certificate proves injectivity; every other instrument is
one-sided and reports collision_found, never injective. certify_injective
returns True or None and never False, because a missing hypothesis is not
evidence against a conclusion. Symmetry recovery is sound and not complete: 6/6
clean, 2/6 at 10% jitter, 0/24 false positives, and every miss is order 1 or a
proper divisor of the truth. The persistent-homology dimension estimator is
trustworthy to roughly intrinsic dimension 3; a uniform 10-D cube reads 8.660 and
degrades with additional samples. so3_scan costs 73.5 s at n=100 and exceeds
300 s at n=500. Every calibrated constant rests on fewer than thirty cases;
FREE_LEVEL was measured not to transfer below n=400 or across dimension and now
refuses to run outside its calibrated range. Most of the benchmark is
two-dimensional while the refutation is for n ≥ 3.

Novelty

None of the mathematics is new: Fekete–Kingman subadditivity, covering-space
theory, mean-value interval hulls, Steele's theorem, Schweinhart's estimator.
Whether any statement is new as a machine-learning instrument went to a
literature sweep whose verdicts, search queries and caveats are in
docs/novelty.md, including a deliberate control (the interval-hull certificate)
that correctly returned already-published. Every "not found" is a not-found over
stated queries, not a proof of absence; two paywalled venues returned HTTP 403
and went unchecked.

Dependencies

numpy, scipy, ripser, persim, mpmath. Python ≥ 3.11. No torch — it was present at
module scope and again inside a function body, carrying eight lines of linear
algebra that numpy provides natively.

References



Gao, Counterexamples to the Jacobian conjecture in dimensions greater than
two, arXiv:2608.00222 (2026)

Lagrange, Delanoue & Jaulin, Reliable Computing 13 (2007), DOI 10.1007/s11155-007-9042-9

Schweinhart, arXiv:1808.02196 · Jaquette & Schweinhart, arXiv:1907.11182

Steele, Growth rates of Euclidean minimal spanning trees, Ann. Probab. (1988)

Sprott, Chaos and Time-Series Analysis, OUP (2003)
